partners.mechanism_chain: CNTN1 (HGNC:2372) —DISRUPTS→ Notch signaling pathway (GO:0007222); DLL4 (HGNC:2109) —DISRUPTS→ Notch signaling pathway (GO:0007222); Notch signaling pathway (GO:0007222) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal vascular development (HP:00114244); Notch signaling pathway (GO:0007222) —LEADS_TO→ Limb malformation (HP:0001873); Notch signaling pathway (GO:0007222) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function mutations in either CNTN1 or DLL4 disrupt the Notch signaling pathway. Dysregulation of this pathway subsequently leads to a spectrum of developmental defects, including abnormal vascular development (relevant to MONDO:0012929) and limb malformations and intellectual disability (relevant to Adams-Oliver syndrome 6, MONDO:0014703).

partners.mechanism_chain: CNTN1 (HGNC:2341) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal neuronal migration (HP:0007364); Abnormal neuronal migration (HP:0007364) —LEADS_TO→ Amyloid precursor protein processing (REACT:R-HSA-1911679); PSEN1 (HGNC:9196) —DISRUPTS→ Amyloid precursor protein processing (REACT:R-HSA-1911679); Amyloid precursor protein processing (REACT:R-HSA-1911679) —INCREASES→ Amyloid plaque formation (HP:0002117); Amyloid plaque formation (HP:0002117) —LEADS_TO→ Dementia (HP:0001249). Loss of function in CNTN1 leads to abnormal neuronal migration, which can indirectly impact brain development and function, potentially contributing to or exacerbating neurodegenerative processes. Gain of function mutations in PSEN1 directly disrupt amyloid precursor protein processing, leading to amyloid plaque formation and downstream neurodegeneration characteristic of Alzheimer's disease. The shared convergence point is the pathway of APP processing, which is affected by both abnormal neuronal development (indirectly) and direct PSEN1 mutations.
